The real threshold variable t bound by integration over [0,∞).

conclusions: E X = ∫_0^∞ P{X > t} dt, using the strict event {X > t}.

definitions_and_conventions: Expectation is the Lebesgue integral over the inherited probability space.
The upper tail is the strict event P{X > t}; the CDF uses X ≤ t.
The threshold integral is a Lebesgue integral with respect to dt.
Indicator notation in the proof is proof evidence, not an additional theorem conclusion.
implicit_context: An underlying probability space (Ω,Σ,P) supplies all event probabilities.
Both nonnegative quantities may take the value infinity; the claim is not restricted to L¹.

details: The result applies to every nonnegative random variable, with no independence, moment, boundedness, or finite-expectation assumption.
The integrand is P{X > t}, not P{X ≥ t}.
The proof confirms the same strict event through 1_{t<X} and P{t<X}.
Thresholds range from 0 to ∞ and integration is with respect to dt.
Fubini-Tonelli in the proof confirms nonnegative Lebesgue-integral semantics including infinity.
The identity has no finiteness premise and the immediately following sentence expressly includes the jointly infinite case.
The theorem-level claims are the displayed identity and simultaneous-finiteness sentence.
The pointwise identity, indicator calculation, interchange, and Tonelli invocation are proof rows, not extra conclusions.

undebatable_constraints: The source hypothesis is nonnegativity of X.
The tail event uses strict X > t.
The threshold integral runs from 0 to ∞ with respect to t.
The left side is E X on the inherited probability space.
No finite-expectation hypothesis may be added because both sides may be infinite.
The simultaneous-finiteness-or-infinity assertion is part of the source contract.
Proof identities and Fubini-Tonelli must not be promoted to extra theorem conclusions.

ambiguities.issue: The source gives no formal codomain to the possibly infinite quantities.
ambiguities.evidence: The lemma uses ordinary equality, while the next sentence says both sides may be infinite.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must preserve the infinite case, for example in extended nonnegative reals; an ordinary real equality alone would omit source content.

contract_plain_english: Every nonnegative real random variable has expectation equal to the Lebesgue integral over t ≥ 0 of P{X > t}. No integrability assumption is made: both sides are finite together or infinite together. The source does not specify pointwise versus almost-sure nonnegativity or a formal type for infinity.
